title: Galois' Dream: Group Theory and Differential Equations
eligibility: Published lectures developed for first-year mathematics students, taking them from elementary notions to using Galois groups in differential equations.
reason: The publisher identifies a structured mathematical teaching purpose. Cartoons, jokes and conceptual connections do not exempt a course text.

eligibility: The author's own website calls this his book in an abridged translation and supplies it for Math480/550. Its opening states the course aim: introduce successive notions of number, related problems and the first steps of their theories.
reason: Identity is established by the author, rather than confused with his different book on fractals. The nominated work is course material with a technical learning purpose.

eligibility: The publisher's subject sequence develops equations of motion, variational principles, Hamiltonian methods and optimal control. The book's own cataloging identifies mechanics, Hamiltonian systems, calculus of variations and control-theory textbooks.
reason: Intuitive derivations and unusual analogies support learning technical mechanics methods; they do not change the primary instructional structure.

eligibility: A technical introduction for senior undergraduates and researchers, developing representation theory, compact and Lie groups and their use in molecular, solid-state and particle physics.
reason: The publisher's audience and sequential theory/application structure establish specialist training and reference as the main purpose.

eligibility: Sternberg's 1969 work is identified in a university library record as notes from a Harvard celestial-mechanics course taught in spring 1968.
reason: The identified nomination is a specialist course text, not a narrative history despite a secondary catalog subject label.

eligibility: A class-tested undergraduate capstone textbook on lattice-point enumeration, with more than 200 exercises and sustained instruction in computational techniques.
reason: Its integration of geometry, combinatorics and number theory is valuable but does not exempt the instructional main purpose.
